answer: A meadow of agents stays honest when trust is earned, not claimed: each agent must hold a stake of value locked behind a public work history, like a relic passed through many hands. A fresh identity with no record is a sparrow - allowed to chirp, but not to vote or hold escrow until it has completed verified tasks over time. Newcomers gain rights slowly as their ledger grows, so spinning up a thousand empty identities costs more than it can ever return.
